lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 104, which makes CI's code review wait for its checking agents before it reports.
lines.say: This is a tour of pull request one oh four, which makes CI's code review wait for its checking agents before it reports.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what the PR adds, how it was checked, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
The prompt now says to wait for every checking agent, and the job fails when the answer or its log shows it didn't.
First, the reviewer runs the code-review skill on the pushed diff, as before.
Then it checks each new finding with its own agent, started together with the next step's agents.
The agents re-checking findings still open from earlier reviews run at the same time, and it waits for all of them.
It returns its output only after every agent has reported, with each answer marked checked.
The collect step then fails the job if any open finding got no answer.
It also fails it when any answer's checked flag is missing or false.
Then it reads the job's execution log, and fails when an agent reported late, or the log is missing.
The comment then says why, nothing is recorded as not fixed, and re-running the review job retries.
On PR #102 the reviewer answered before its agents reported, so that PR needed six review rounds.
lines.say: On pull request one oh two the reviewer answered before its agents reported, so that pull request needed six review rounds.

lines.caption: It wasn't a timeout. The agents ran in the background, and nothing told the reviewer to wait.
Step 2 starts both batches of agents in one message, with background off, and waits for every one before the fix.
Step 4 returns an answer for every open finding, each with a checked flag that is true only if its agent reported.
Steps 5 and 6 check the answer: every open id answered, every answer checked. The wording isn't read.
Background agents are told by their launch result. No agents for real findings, or no readable log, also fails.
The findings and fix are still saved, and the code review comment names the reason and asks for a re-run.
Here are the checks: missing answers, unchecked answers, a missing log, late agents, and no agents at all.
The wording is never read, so a note that quotes an agent not reporting passes when its agent did report.
The review script changes, with the log check, one line of the workflow uploads the reason, plus this page and its narration.
To undo it, revert the one commit.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
The checks were tried in dry runs with fake output and logs. CI's fifth review ran the log check on a real log.
lines.say: The checks were tried in dry runs with fake output and logs. C I's fifth review ran the log check on a real log.

lines.caption: #102's own reviews show answers handed in before their agents reported, which the checked flag now records.
lines.say: One oh two's own reviews show answers handed in before their agents reported, which the checked flag now records.

lines.caption: The prompt already ran agents in parallel. The PR starts both batches together and adds the wait.
The log check follows the Claude action's documented output format, and CI's fifth review showed the real log matches it.
lines.say: The log check follows the Claude action's documented output format, and C I's fifth review showed the real log matches it.

lines.caption: After the wording check was dropped, a dry run with an open finding left unanswered failed.
A new finding left unchecked, one with no checked field, and an unchecked open finding all failed.
A checked finding that quotes #102's not-reported wording now passes.
lines.say: A checked finding that quotes one oh two's not-reported wording now passes.

lines.caption: A review with nothing open passed too, but only before the first fix round.
A stray old id was ignored, and earlier, a lower-case id still matched.
A previous entry with no id no longer stops the collect step.
With hand-made logs, a background agent that never reported, a late report, and a wrong agent id all failed.
A log where every agent reported passed, ignoring a subagent's own nested call.
On the latest fix, an agent left in the background by default that never reported failed.
A log with no agents, while there were findings to check, failed too.
A missing log and an unreadable one now fail. On the R23 commit they only warned.
lines.say: A missing log and an unreadable one now fail. On the R twenty-three commit they only warned.

lines.caption: Good logs still passed, including one with no agents when there was nothing to check.
On CI's real log, the check counted 9 agent calls, none late, so the format matched.
lines.say: On C I's real log, the check counted nine agent calls, none late, so the format matched.

lines.caption: The screenshot audit of 128 shots from this PR's build passed. This PR changes no Thunar code.
lines.say: The screenshot audit of a hundred and twenty-eight shots from this pull request's build passed. This pull request changes no Thunar code.

lines.caption: Re-running the review at #102's head was not run. That PR belongs to another session.
lines.say: Re-running the review at one oh two's head was not run. That pull request belongs to another session.

lines.caption: A fresh agent also reviewed the latest fix, and found nothing.
A fresh agent found one problem, fixed. Two later ones found three low notes each. The latest found nothing.
The first wording check also matched ordinary sentences. It was narrowed, then dropped.
It checked the rest and found it fine.
The second review's notes widened the wording and limited the checked rule to the findings that matter.
The third review's gaps widened the wording again, before it was dropped.
CI's first review found R1 to R9. R1, a confirmed medium, failed the review job.
Now a failed collect keeps its findings and fix, and the comment says why it failed.
Answers carry the checked flag, and ids match whatever their case or spacing.
Both batches of agents now start together, so the fix has every verdict.
R9 was disproved by the review itself, and you accepted it.

lines.caption: Part 3. What comes later.
No open issue builds on this one. The next reviews are the test.
Every finding gets checked before the report, so you should see fewer review rounds.
In short: the review now waits for its agents, or fails and is re-run.
